data.narrative:
MatX, a Series B semiconductor company founded by Reiner Pope and Mike Gunter, has raised $500M+ to date. Valuation analysis draws from a peer set of 8 private and 3 public comparables in the Chips & Semiconductors sector, including same-stage and adjacent-stage companies such as Positron AI ($1.0B Series B), d-Matrix ($2.0B Series A), and Rebellions ($2.3B Series A).

Two methods produce actionable estimates. Stage-progression, applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier to the $500M total raised proxy, yields $950M. Peer-median analysis across the 5-company sample delivers $2.0B, with a range spanning $529M (DEEPX, Series C) to $11.0B (SambaNova, Series A). Public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) trade at a 18.4x price-to-sales median but cannot be applied; MatX's revenue remains undisclosed, as is typical for private frontier-tech companies.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $808M to $2.3B, with a median of $1.5B. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around timing of inflection to positive unit economics, competitive differentiation versus well-capitalized incumbents, and the stage dynamics of the peer set itself. Stage-progression yields the floor; peer-median anchors the midpoint. Critical data gaps—revenue run rate, gross margins, and customer concentration—would narrow this range materially.
